segments.heading: One box, many eyes
lines: One box, many eyes.

segments.heading: The shortcut and the check
lines: Here is a box on a floor, lit from one side. Real-time engines darken the creases with a cheap trick called screen-space ambient occlusion.
raw-native draws the trick, and then it draws the slow answer by tracing rays, and measures how far apart the two are.
For this view the gap is 0.129, against a tolerance of 0.120. The certificate says refuted.

predict.question: The shortcut looks right. Is it inside the tolerance?
predict.status: pending the author's script decision: held as a 2.5 s silent still, the question not shown or spoken

segments.heading: Same bytes, every build
lines: The same render comes out byte for byte the same from three compilers and from the WebAssembly build.
The film you are watching is drawn the same way: every frame is a function of time alone. Rendered twice, 1,456 frames matched exactly.

segments.heading: Lines and colour
lines: The box's outline is drawn as vector paths. Over 20 test drawings, the average edge error against a slow reference stays under 0.028 in every one.

Light brighter than a screen can show goes through a tone mapper. The GPU matches its own C++ reference within 1 step in 255, and the C++ version of ACES 2.0 matches OpenColorIO within a colour difference of 0.0024.

segments.heading: A tube, simulated as a tube
lines: Now the same box on an old television. raw-native does not paint scanlines on. It encodes the picture as a broadcast signal, decodes it the way a television did, and fires simulated electron beams at a phosphor mask.
Dot crawl and rainbow fringes appear because the decoder gets things wrong, the way a real one did.
Across 9 tube settings, the GPU matches the slow CPU version within 1 step in 255.

segments.heading: Film, simulated as film
lines: On film, the box exposes a negative through three layers, is developed, printed and projected.
Grain comes from a published model of how silver clouds form, and the red halo around bright light comes from light bouncing inside the film base.
segments.claim_tag: most film and tube constants: low confidence

segments.heading: Paint, tape, pixels and what landed
lines: The same box, painted. The paint pass turns each colour into amounts of four real pigments, so blue and yellow brushed together make green, the way paint does.
On a videotape, the picture goes through a simulated tape head: detail washes out, colour smears behind the edges, and the bottom lines skip where the heads switch.

As pixel art, the box stays still while the camera turns. In the library's test, under one pixel in ten thousand changed colour as the view moved, against up to 19 percent for simply rendering small and scaling up.
And with an old sixteen-colour palette and dither, the GPU picks the same colour as the slow version for every one of 16,777,216 inputs.
Models from other tools now load: ten glTF models render on the CPU and on the GPU, and each GPU frame is verified against the CPU.
Wobbling retro geometry is checked against a CPU twin: across 12 cases, no pixel away from an edge is covered by a different triangle.
And the box can now be fully lit. Over 55,270 test points, the clustered lights missed none that the full list found.

segments.heading: One thing to keep
lines: One thing to keep: a style is a claim, and every claim here comes with the test that could say no.
The voice you heard is a synthesized version of mine. Every number on screen links to its source under the video.
